title: Montreal Canadiens acquire centre Dylan Larkin from Red Wings in blockbuster trade
summary: The Red Wings traded centre Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal on Sunday, ending a drawn-out saga after Detroit's former captain requested a move in the off-season.

image.caption: Red Wings centre Dylan Larkin is shown during a game against the Seattle Kraken in Detroit on Oct. 9. (Paul Sancya/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: The Red Wings traded centre Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal on Sunday, ending a drawn-out saga after Detroit's former captain requested a move in the off-season.
Larkin's move fills a need that has lingered near the top of Montreal's wish list

The Canadiens sent the Red Wings a major package that includes forward Kirby Dach, goalie Sam Montembeault and highly touted prospect Michael Hage. Detroit also receives a first-round draft pick in 2027, a second-round pick in 2027, a fourth-round pick in 2028 and a first-round pick in 2029.
Along with Larkin, the Habs acquired the Red Wings' second-round pick in 2028 and their third-round pick in 2027.
The move fills a need that has lingered near the top of Montreal's wish list for more than a year.
Larkin slots in behind Nick Suzuki to give the Canadiens a legitimate second-line centre.
